Jason Silva's episode 194 of the Joe Rogan Experience is an early trip from the show's first years. Silva is a futurist performer who delivers wonder in short, intense bursts, a style fans call shots of philosophical espresso. With Rogan, he gets hours instead of minutes.

The talk runs across technology, awe, and the human upgrade Silva loves to preach. Rogan feeds him questions and rides the waves of his answers. The episode has an old-school energy. Two young men in a small room talk their way toward the edge of the future, and it charms for exactly that reason.
podcast-tuckercarlson-VlcGvv-HKJc:
British politician Rupert Lowe warns Tucker Carlson that democracy in Britain has gone badly wrong. Voters, he says, get the same result from every party. He calls his country the mother of parliaments.

Lowe argues that a global agenda is hollowing out the West. The title warns of revolution if nothing changes. He and Carlson compare Britain with the United States. Both see voters who feel ignored by leaders. The episode gives an American audience a stark British version of a complaint they hear at home every day. His warning is blunt: change course or lose the nation.
